setup: Same frozen frames on both renderers in an emulated iPhone: 844×390 landscape, DPR 3, touch, iPhone Safari user agent (so phone memory caps apply), LOW resolution (0.5) by default and MED 0.75 + UPSCALE where marked. TLX runs three's WebGL2 path, which is what an iPhone runs. Software-rendered stills and memory; frame time from the one real GPU we can reach (the CI Mac, with phone caps forced).
recommendation: Make GLX the phone default; keep TLX one tap away in RENDERER. On the same phone settings GLX holds about 30 MB less at the menu and 42–53 MB less in a race (heap + ArrayBuffers, software box), and 59 MB less JS heap on the real-GPU Mac (74.5 vs 133.7 MiB). That is the three.js geometry-copy cost the code already warns has jetsam-killed an iPhone tab. On the Mac GPU with phone caps, GLX ran 24.9 fps at its full quality tier, where TLX had to shed to tier 3 and 0.8 scale for 25.9 fps. GLX entered the race in 5.9 s against 19.1 s. The look is close: 2–14% of pixels differ in matched frames. GLX shows more, not less: it draws clouds and night stars that TLX drops on the phone tier, and its edges are smoother in the garage. The cost is two renderers kept first-class. Every look fix must land in both, and TLX stays the path for Android WebGPU and desktop. GLX's one worse number is a single 1.4 s block during race entry, against 0.5 s on TLX.
tiles: GLX vs TLX, post-GC heap + ArrayBuffers
GLX vs TLX, race() to track ready
memNote: Chromium in this container, phone profile (iPhone UA → mobileTier, DPR 3, LOW 0.5). Each row is three forced GCs, then Runtime.getHeapUsage. JS heap plus ArrayBuffer backing stores (≈ DevTools JSArrayBufferData). It matches performance.memory to within 1 MB. Each race is __apex.race(id) and go(), sampled after 10 s of racing. One browser per backend. GPU memory is not included.
perfNote: Frame time from gpu-census.yml on macos-latest. That is a paravirtual Apple GPU, not an iPhone, but it is the only real GPU the project can reach. The run forced phone caps (apex26.forceMobileTier=1) on Monza, helmet cam, with a 20 s autopilot window and the governor live. Local SwiftShader frame times at phone DPR collapsed to 0.2–0.4 fps on both renderers, with and without the 4× CPU throttle, so they carry no signal and are not shown. For a true phone number, Bryce's on-phone PHONE TEST › GPU TEST would do.
gapNote: A code read of both trees with mobileTier on, checked against the stills. Most phone gates are set once in game.js, so they apply to both renderers. Nothing a player sees on a phone exists only in TLX. What TLX has alone are cost caps.

stillsNote: Each frame was frozen on both renderers with the same camera. Diff counts pixels whose summed RGB moved by more than 30. HUD overlays such as radio toasts sometimes land in only one frame, so read the crops, not just the number. The start grid and the MED helmet frame are left out. TLX's race entry is slower, so its start sequence put the car back on the grid after the camera was placed. Those frames compared different moments, not different renderers.
